Permutation-calibrated score test for an exposure in a GLM

Source: R/perglm_test.R
perglm_test.Rd

Test for an exposure contribution to a conditional mean using an empirically studentized GLM score and a fixed number of marginal exposure permutations. The null model is fitted once; its working scores, weights and projection factors are reused across permutations.

Usage

perglm_test(
  formula,
  data,
  exposure,
  family = stats::gaussian(),
  B = 999L,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  batch_size = 64L,
  keep_statistics = FALSE,
  control = stats::glm.control(),
  tol = 1e-07
)

Arguments

formula

A two-sided null-model formula containing the response and nuisance covariates only. Include an intercept and exclude the exposure. Fixed offsets can be included with offset().

data

A data frame containing the null-model observations.

exposure

A finite real numeric vector with one value per row of data, in the same order. This argument is evaluated normally: use exposure = dat$x, rather than a bare column name or a character string. If named, names must exactly match the null-model row names.

family

A supported GLM family object, zero-argument constructor or factory, or family name. The default is stats::gaussian().

B

A positive integer number of permutations; defaults to 999L.

alternative

One of "two.sided" (default), "greater", or "less". One-sided alternatives refer to the exposure coefficient on the link scale.

batch_size

A positive integer maximum number of exposure permutations scored together. Smaller batches reduce working memory.

keep_statistics

Whether to retain the permuted statistics in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

control

A list of fitting controls accepted by stats::glm.control().

tol

Relative tolerance for the nuisance-design rank check and residual exposure identifiability, strictly between zero and one.

Value

An object of class "htest", printed using the standard R method, with components:

statistic

The signed empirically studentized score, named T.

parameter

The permutation budget, named B.

p.value

The permutation p-value.

null.value

The null exposure coefficient, zero.

alternative

The alternative hypothesis.

method

A description including the working family and link.

data.name

The exposure expression and null-model formula.

B, exceedances

The number of draws and their exceedance count.

nobs

The number of model observations.

family, link, theta

The working family name, link, and negative-binomial size (NULL for other families).

null_diagnostics

Null-fit convergence, iterations, and maximum normalized nuisance score, plus separation_checked and gaussian_residual_check. The latter contains residual_norm, roundoff_bound, and relative_residual_norm for Gaussian fits; otherwise it is NULL.

permuted_statistics

The sampled scores if keep_statistics = TRUE, otherwise NULL.

No full model fit, coefficient estimate, or confidence interval is retained.

Details

The working alternative adds an exposure term to the linear predictor, \(g(\mu_i) = Z_i^T\beta + \gamma X_i + \mathrm{offset}_i\). The null hypothesis is \(\gamma = 0\). The alternatives "greater" and "less" use the positive and negative signed-score tails, respectively. With a decreasing link, a positive exposure coefficient corresponds to a lower conditional mean.

Supported working families are Gaussian, Bernoulli (binomial), Poisson, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, and negative binomial, with their standard named links. Binomial responses must be coded as zero or one. Grouped binomial counts, prior weights, missing model observations, and rank-deficient or intercept-free nuisance designs are not supported. The null fit must converge to an interior solution and have positive residual degrees of freedom. The exposure must have identifiable residual variation. Bernoulli fits require both outcome values; count fits require at least one positive outcome. A constant response with a constant offset gives zero empirical score variance and is rejected.

During null preparation, Bernoulli designs are checked once for complete or quasi-complete separation using detectseparation::detect_separation(). The check uses the geometry of the free nuisance design, excluding fixed offsets, and applies to every supported binomial link. Separated designs cannot have an interior likelihood optimum and are rejected. The requested working link and ordinary maximum-likelihood fitting procedure are preserved.

Gaussian fits are checked once for residuals indistinguishable from fitting roundoff. The numerical envelope follows the response, fitted means and inverse-link derivative times absolute linear-predictor products. It scales with measurement units and accounts for cancellation in the prediction. This is a numerical-resolution diagnostic, not a statistical minimum-noise threshold or a certificate for arbitrarily ill-conditioned fits.

Supply family = "negative.binomial" to estimate the size parameter using MASS::glm.nb() with a log link. Supply a MASS::negative.binomial() family object to use a fixed size parameter. Common dispersion factors cancel from empirical studentization.

Each draw independently and uniformly permutes the raw exposure labels. Repeated permutations and the identity permutation are allowed. Exposure residuals and empirical score variance are recomputed for every draw while the null-model quantities remain fixed. Inclusive tail comparisons give \(p = (1 + K)/(B + 1)\), where \(K\) is the exceedance count. Two-sided comparisons use absolute scores, and the smallest attainable p-value is \(1/(B+1)\).

Use set.seed() before calling the function for reproducibility. Successful runs give identical results and final RNG states across batch sizes and retention settings. If an observed or sampled score is undefined, including zero empirical variance or numerical nuisance aliasing, the function stops without a p-value. Draws are never discarded or redrawn.

Conditional-mean inference follows the paper under a correct null mean model and its regularity conditions; the working outcome variance may be misspecified. The procedure does not test all forms of conditional dependence.

References

Ai, J. and Niu, Z. (2026). Conditional independence testing through marginal permutation. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2611.03255 .

Examples

set.seed(42)
dat <- data.frame(z1 = rnorm(120), z2 = rnorm(120),
                  x = rbinom(120, 1, 0.3))
dat$y <- rpois(120, exp(0.3 + 0.2 * dat$z1 - 0.1 * dat$z2 + 0.2 * dat$x))

set.seed(2026)
result <- perglm_test(y ~ z1 + z2, data = dat, exposure = dat$x,
                      family = stats::poisson(), B = 99L)
result
#> 
#> 	Permutation-calibrated GLM score test (poisson, log link)
#> 
#> data:  dat$x with null model y ~ z1 + z2
#> T = 1.6236, B = 99, p-value = 0.12
#> alternative hypothesis: true exposure coefficient is not equal to 0
#> 
result$p.value
#> [1] 0.12
